subject: Turks and Caicos anole
title: Scientists Measured These Lizards 4 Days Before a Hurricane Hit

scenes.text: Two hurricanes accidentally ran a perfect experiment on these lizards.
Scientists measured anole lizards on two tiny islands in Turks and Caicos.
Four days later, Hurricane Irma hit. Two weeks after that, Maria.
Six weeks on, the survivors had front toe pads about nine percent bigger, and back legs six percent shorter.
A leaf blower showed why. They cling with their front feet, and long back legs catch wind like a sail.
Two storms, six weeks, and the lizards had a better grip.

description:
Researchers had just measured anole lizards on Pine Cay and Water Cay in Turks and Caicos when Hurricane Irma hit four days later, followed by Hurricane Maria.
The survivors had front toe pads about 9% larger and hind legs about 6% shorter. Leaf-blower tests showed long back legs catch the wind and are the first to lose grip. The study was published in Nature.
Would you have guessed the legs mattered most?
first_comment: The leaf-blower lizards weren't hurt: each one was blown into a padded net and released where it was caught. What should scientists test with a leaf blower next?
